units: Adaptive Inheritance is an implementation and evaluation framework for measuring whether empirical consequences retain causal authority over adaptive systems.
The central evaluation question is whether reality can modify mechanisms responsible for future behavior when assumptions become invalid.
Adaptive Corrigibility is defined as the measurable capacity of a system's future mechanism distribution to be causally altered by unblocked empirical consequences.
AIC: E* implies there exists an invalid mechanism weight w_i whose time derivative is negative.
E* denotes unblocked empirical contradiction; w_i denotes the causal authority of an active mechanism.
Invalidated mechanisms must lose future influence; adaptive corrigibility requires empirical consequences to retain causal influence over mechanisms generating future behavior.
The README does not provide an identification procedure establishing that stored mechanism weights are measures of future causal authority rather than implementation variables.
Adaptive Inheritance is not a claim that all intelligent systems are necessarily corrigible; it defines and measures one adaptive property.
Adaptive corrigibility is treated as an empirical control characteristic rather than a normative assumption.
Adaptive Corrigibility is distinguished from shutdownability, instruction obedience, acceptance of human intervention, and preference alignment.
The framework is organized as a five-layer adaptive control stack: PTVS telemetry, MRAT controller, Adaptive Inheritance, REE, and RAHU, driven by an empirical shift E*.
PTVS is described as Polynomial-Time Verification Schemas providing local trajectory admissibility telemetry.
LBR_t is the ratio of inadmissible trajectories to total trajectories.
PTVS is intended to identify where candidate mechanisms lose empirical admissibility by evaluating intermediate trajectories rather than only final outputs.
The README does not define a domain-general trajectory generator, environmental admissibility criterion, sampling protocol, or independence assumptions for LBR.
MRAT is the Minimal Residual Attribution Test that routes observed failures to the lowest-cost structural layer capable of correction.
The routing operator maps residual e_t to attribution components a_N, a_S, a_M, a_R, a_G corresponding to Noise, State error, Mechanism deficit, Representation saturation, and Generator decoupling.
The source orders intervention costs C_noise < C_state < C_mechanism < C_representation < C_generator.
MRAT is intended to determine what level of internal structure must change.
The README does not specify how attribution components are causally identified or calibrated, nor how heterogeneous adaptation costs are put on a common scale.
The Adaptive Inheritance Engine maintains mechanism authority weights W_t = {w_1,...,w_n} and applies empirical attenuation.
The authority update is w_i^(t+1) = w_i^t(1 - lambda(1 - A_adm,i)).
Primary proposed measures are Authority Retention Ratio, Mechanism Authority Half-Life, and satisfaction of the Adaptive Inheritance Criterion.
The README does not define an empirical estimator for A_adm, lambda selection, normalization of W, or a causal intervention demonstrating that w_i corresponds to operational future influence.
Recursive Representation Expansion is a gated representation-expansion mechanism and is explicitly not an automatic response to failure.
REE requires estimated bounded-search residual saturation Gamma_hat_B^max approximately equal to e_t and estimated future adaptive gain exceeding representation cost.
Representation expansion is permitted only when lower-cost explanations are insufficient, current representation capacity is saturated, and additional structure has measurable adaptive value.
The README does not specify estimators for bounded residual compressibility, future adaptive gain, representation cost, or the approximate-equality threshold in the REE gate.
RAHU is the Reality-Adversarial Hypothesis Updating benchmark for evaluating adaptive behavior under controlled contradiction.
RAHU is intended to measure whether invalidated mechanisms lose operational influence after empirical failure.
RAHU observables named by the README are LBR, C_post, R_update, V_corr, ARR, ADI, ACS, and tau_adapt.

The source assigns LBR to empirical friction, Phi_R to failure attribution, ARR to invalid-authority retention, ADI to adaptive decoupling, ACS to composite adaptive corrigibility, tau_adapt to structural response speed, and V_corr to correction magnitude per contradiction.
The README names benchmark observables but does not establish their construct validity, calibration, sampling distributions, or acceptance thresholds.
The source describes docs, five src subpackages, and four test modules as the repository structure.
The research goal distinguishes task capability under a world model from whether the world can change that world model.
The repository describes itself as an early research implementation.
Current focus includes formalizing inheritance dynamics, implementing MRAT routing, building RAHU synthetic environments, testing authority decay, and validating separability from static capability.
The current-status wording is not itself evidence that the named testing or validation activities have been executed or completed.
Architecture Specification defines the software architecture intended to implement Adaptive Inheritance.
The architectural objective is E* -> Phi_R(e_t) -> Delta W -> W_(t+1).
The architecture separates constraint-failure detection, residual attribution, authority redistribution, representation-expansion gating, and empirical validation.
AIC requires at least one invalidated mechanism authority weight to decrease over time after empirical evidence invalidates an active mechanism.
The architecture does not require immediate mechanism replacement; it requires invalidated mechanisms to lose inherited influence.
The specified processing order is Environment Reality -> E* -> PTVS -> MRAT -> Adaptive Inheritance -> REE -> RAHU.
PTVS is assigned responsibility for detecting local violations between generated trajectories and environmental constraints and is specified not to modify mechanisms.
The specified PTVS signal is LBR = inadmissible trajectories / total generated trajectories.
PTVS interface is specified to take TrajectoryBatch and EnvironmentConstraints and output PTVSReport.
The architecture gives an illustrative PTVS JSON report with timestamp, violation count, total paths, and LBR.
Illustrative example is not an execution record.
MRAT is assigned responsibility for determining the lowest structural level responsible for observed failure and preventing unnecessary structural modification.
MRAT routing maps e_t to an attribution vector a=(a_N,a_S,a_M,a_R,a_G) with components summing to 1.
MRAT interface is specified to take ResidualSignal, PTVSReport, and CurrentMechanism and output AttributionVector.
The architecture gives an illustrative attribution vector dominated by mechanism attribution.
Illustrative example is not a reported observation.
Adaptive Inheritance is assigned responsibility for modifying mechanism authority based on empirical validity.
The architecture maintains W_t={w_1,...,w_n}, with each w_i described as future causal influence.
ARR is specified as w_invalid^post / w_invalid^pre.
Authority half-life is the earliest time at which invalid authority falls to at most half its initial value.
REE is assigned responsibility for representation expansion only when lower-order adaptation is insufficient.
Specified REE admissibility requires residual saturation and expected future adaptive gain greater than representation cost; otherwise expansion is rejected.
RAHU is assigned external empirical-validation responsibility using Agent, Environment, and TelemetryStack inputs and RAHUReport output.
The architecture source asserts a module dependency flow ptvs -> mrat -> inheritance, with inheritance feeding ree and rahu.
Source relation assertion does not emit a Cerebro map edge.
The system is required to operate using externally observable behavior without chain-of-thought access.
The architecture requires minimizing adaptation cost subject to restoring empirical coupling.
Performance and corrigibility are specified as separate axes; high performance can coexist with ARR approximately 1.

A successful implementation is required to demonstrate contradiction detection, residual attribution, authority redistribution, parsimonious structural modification, and measurable reduction of invalid mechanism influence.
The architecture is considered validated when E* -> Phi_R(e_t) -> Delta W -> W_(t+1) is observable through external telemetry.
The document describes the architecture as a paper-to-code contract without premature commitment to implementation details.
The architecture specifies an interface but not a domain-general method for trajectory generation or constraint construction.
The architecture does not supply an identification method mapping residual observations to causal N/S/M/R/G attribution mass.
The architecture calls w_i future causal influence but does not define an empirical intervention or counterfactual estimator establishing that interpretation.
The architecture leaves the estimators and common scale for residual saturation, future gain, and representation cost unspecified.
The architecture specifies composite metrics but does not establish their empirical calibration or construct validity.
